control.runs: ADR v2.2: Delegated = external_client/connection_scoped (client connections; control-connection loss stops it); Durable = platform/platform_durable (created inside the Runtime only; no connection ends it)
control.lease: one per Desktop, held by one live Run
control.admission: runtime.stopAll closes input for all Runs; runtime.enableInput reopens for new Runs only

methods.note: not ledgered: the attach token it returns is a credential and must not be stored; a retry starts another Run, which ends with its connection

A6: starts a GUI unit Run (kind unit) on the RunStore. From a connection it is always a Delegated Run (external_client / connection_scoped / agent_hub); the main window starts Durable gui_explorer Runs in-process, never on the wire. origin / lifetime / ownership in params are refused with ownership_escalation_denied (details.reason ownership_from_params). Every admission check (F40-06) runs before the Run exists; a refusal creates no Run and the ledger replays it for the same requestId. Listed in runtime.capabilities only while a GUI executor is registered; without one the answer is unsupported_backend (reason gui_execution_off). Progress is in the Run's events (unit.*, UnitRunEvent) and Run.unit; read, wait, stop with run.show / run.wait / run.cancel / run.events.

after the reply the server pushes EventFrame lines on this connection; other methods are refused there until events.unsubscribe. With runId: that Run from sequence `after` (default 0), and the server closes the connection once the Run has ended and every event was sent. Without: every visible Run, global cursor `after` (default: now). Closing never affects a Run.

owner; closes this Desktop's input admission and stops the Run holding it (any origin, closingReason desktop_stop); the receipt separates accepted from quiescent: run.phase stopping / quiescence pending while an action of it is in flight. New Runs on the Desktop are refused (input_disabled, details.reason desktop_stopped) until desktop.handback; other Desktops are untouched; a paired client gets permission_denied, reason owner_only

owner; manual takeover: closes agents' admission on the Desktop, stops the Run holding it (closingReason takeover) and, once nothing of it is in flight, starts a platform Run of origin user (kind exec, platform_durable) that holds the lease; every other Run is refused (control_busy, details.reason manual_control); Desktop.control.state manual. While the stopped Run still finishes an action past the deadline: stop_pending (retryable, notSent false: the takeover was accepted and admission stays closed), ask again with a new requestId. A takeover that waited while the owner handed the Desktop back or stopped it does nothing (conflict, details.reason superseded). Taking over a Desktop already taken over answers its Run again; a paired client gets permission_denied, reason owner_only

owner; ends the user's Run (closingReason handback, outcome success), reopens the Desktop's admission (after desktop.takeover or desktop.stop) and forgets every observation of the Desktop: an agent observes again before acting and nothing queued before is replayed; it also clears a Desktop its last Run left stopped, disconnected or unknown (the Run itself keeps its outcome); on a ready Desktop, one an agent's Run holds, or under a global stop (runtime.enableInput lifts that) nothing changes (handedBack false); a paired client gets permission_denied, reason owner_only

owner; what desktop.destroy would do now, changing nothing: blockers (the Run holding the Desktop, open sessions; canClose false while any), the processes it would ask to quit (app.launch started them here and they still run) and the ones whose windows stay (not launched here: the user's own apps lent by window.bind or shown there; everything on a physical Desktop, whose display is kept); a paired client gets permission_denied, reason owner_only

desktop.manage; ends one process app.launch started on this Desktop (a paired client: one it launched itself), never the user's own apps: anything else is permission_denied, reason not_launched_here, naming nothing; a Run of another client holding the Desktop: control_busy (the owner may quit regardless). Asks the app to quit and waits up to 3 s: exited true once the process is gone (it leaves the Desktop's launches and its binding, if bound), else exited false (asked, not proof)

desktop.manage; a virtual Desktop's size, changed in place (320x240 up to what the display reserved; beyond: execution_failed); a physical Desktop is invalid_target; a Run of another client holding the Desktop: control_busy (the owner may resize regardless). Every observation of the Desktop is forgotten: act on an older snapshot is stale_observation

observe; the write requests the Runtime accepted (the request ledger, 7 days), newest first, each exactly as request.show gives it plus clientId and the desktopId it named (params.desktopId, else its session's or Run's Desktop; none for records older than A5 or naming none); filters method, state, desktopId, since, and for the owner clientId (the owner sees every caller's records, a paired client only its own; a paired client's desktopId must be in its grant); limit 1–100 (default 50), cursor from next; a page ends early rather than exceed 768 KiB

authorization.principal: from the handshake credential only: owner (the host's in-process connections; no socket client is ever the owner), paired app (app:<id> credential from hub.pairing; a client that paired as verified code must satisfy its designated requirement, read from the socket's audit token, on every handshake), else unpaired
authorization.unpaired: runtime.handshake, runtime.capabilities, hub.pairing.start, hub.pairing.status; anything else is pairing_required
authorization.paired: runtime.status (counts only what it may see), and each method its grant covers: observe (desktop/app/window lists, observe, wait, artifacts, session.show, request.show), act (act, session.open/close), desktop.manage (desktop create/destroy/resize, app.launch/quit, window bind/unbind), run (run.*, events.*, and runtime.stopAll, which stops only its own Runs and leaves input admission as it is), unit.run; Desktops in grant.desktops or "created" ones it created; apps in grant.apps. runtime.enableInput, ai.*, hub.clients.*, hub.grants.*, hub.connections.list: one call at a time, each confirmed by the user in the trusted window, and only for a client whose code identity is verified, except calls that only take access away (revoke, narrowing grants.set); never for the caller's own grant (self_grant). hub.displays.* (attaching one of the user's displays for a client, and taking it back) is the owner's alone and is never asked for by a client. Everything else is the owner's (permission_denied, reason owner_only, or the seal's reasons launch_requires_grant, window_discovery_requires_grant, bind_requires_grant, gui_run_requires_grant)
authorization.checked: every request, against the client and grant as they are now; an action once more right before its input goes out
authorization.pairing: hub.pairing.start asks the user in the host's trusted window (details, short code, user authentication); approved exactly as shown, the grant's duration counting from the approval; denied, cancelled, timed out or no trusted window: denied
authorization.confirmation: a confirmation is bound to a digest of exactly what will be applied, recomputed by the window from what it displayed; params are shown in full and a call too large to show is refused unseen; refusals: permission_denied with reason user_denied, user_cancelled, confirmation_timeout, confirmation_busy, confirmation_mismatch, confirmation_too_large, pairing_busy or no_trusted_ui
authorization.targets: every Desktop, session and Run a paired client's request names, in its context or params, is authorized; naming two different Desktops is invalid_argument (reason target_mismatch)
authorization.handshake: a socket connection completes runtime.handshake once (conflict, reason already_handshaken)
authorization.windowGrants: docs/security/window-grants.md: a paired client reaches a window it did not launch itself on that Desktop only through a window grant (window ID + process launch + app + Desktop + client), each one confirmed by the user; observe, act and persist are separate; every use is checked against the grant as it is now (bind, both observe steps, each wait poll, act right before dispatch, artifact reads); a grant ends for good when the window closes, its process or app changes, its Desktop goes or the Runtime restarts, or the app or Desktop leaves the client's grant; window.list shows a paired client only windows it holds a grant for and windows of processes it launched; without persist an observation's screenshot is transient (120 s, deleted when the grant ends)
authorization.policy: iPhone Mirroring (com.apple.ScreenContinuity) is refused for every principal, the owner included, until the iPhone device session is accepted (#139): app.launch by bundle id or by a path in its bundle, window.bind of its process, and observe, act and wait on a binding to it answer permission_denied with reason iphone_mirroring_blocked, before anything is captured, read, sent, moved or recorded as a success. This is a security-policy refusal, not a missing grant: no grant, capability or pairing lifts it. Fail closed: a process is identified by the running-app list and by the bundle of its executable; when neither can tell, it is refused the same way with details.identity unverified (otherwise iphone_mirroring), for that request only, and the next request identifies it anew. A launched process found to be it, or unidentified, is never kept as the Desktop's app; it is asked to quit only because app.launch returns a process its launch token proved it started (never by time or list), and details.quitRequested says whether it was asked (a request, not proof that it exited). A launch that could not prove its process fails with the engine's own error and nothing is quit
authorization.displays: docs/security/owner-display-attach.md: only the owner, in the Agent Desktop window, attaches one of the user's displays as a physical Desktop and lists it in a paired client's grant (hub.displays.attach, confirmed by the user with Touch ID or the login password); a display is attachable only when the Runtime proved it physical (built in, or an external display matched one-to-one to a hardware framebuffer); the attached Desktop gives the client no window: each window still needs a window grant; hub.displays.detach takes it back, ending the client's window grants on it; desktop.create {physical} from a paired client stays permission_denied, reason owner_only
